On renyin Wei Chang, prefect of Henan, was made military commissioner of Pinglu, and Gao Kai, Vice Minister of Punishments, was made prefect of Henan. On jiachen Cui Dan, Grandee of the Palace, acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Pillar of State, and recipient of the purple-gold fish bag, was authorized to serve as Grand Councillor while retaining his current offices. Cang-Jing and Zi-Qing suffered major floods.
165
八月庚戌朔，以給事中姚合為陝虢觀察使。 辛亥，鄜王憬薨。 丙辰，邢州廢青山縣，磁州移昭義縣於固鎮驛。 癸亥，以左僕射牛僧孺檢校司空、同平章事，兼襄州刺史，充山南東道節度使。 辛未夜，流星出羽林，尾長八十餘尺，滅後有聲如雷。 壬申，鎮、冀四州蝗食稼，至於野草樹葉皆盡。
On the gengxu new moon of the eighth month, Yao He, Supervising Secretary, was made Shan-Guo observation commissioner. On xinhai Prince Jing of Fu died. On bingchen Xingzhou abolished Qingshan County, and Cizhou moved Zhaoyi County to Guzhen Station. On guihai Niu Sengru, Left Vice Director, was made acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor, concurrently prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East. On the night of xinwei a meteor emerged from Yulin, its tail more than eighty chi long; after it vanished there was a sound like thunder. On renshen locusts in the four prefectures of Zhen and Ji ate the crops until even wild grasses and tree leaves were gone.
166
九月己卯朔。 辛卯，以劍南東川節度楊汝士為吏部侍郎。 丁酉夜，月掩東井第三星。 辛丑，以吏部侍郎陳夷行為華州鎮國軍防禦使，以蘇州刺史李穎為江西觀察使，以諫議大夫馮定為桂管觀察使。 甲辰，以京兆尹鄭復為劍南東川節度使。 丙午，以前江西觀察使敬昕為京兆尹。
The ninth month opened on jimao. On xinmao Yang Rushi, military commissioner of Jiannan Dongchuan, was made Vice Minister of Personnel. On the night of dingyou the moon covered the third star of Dongjing. On xinchou Chen Yixing, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made defense commissioner of the Zhenguo Army at Huazhou; Li Ying, prefect of Suzhou, was made Jiangxi observation commissioner; and Feng Ding, Grand Master for Remonstrance, was made Gui-Guan observation commissioner. On jiachen Zheng Fu, Jingzhao Prefect, was made military commissioner of Jiannan Dongchuan. On bingwu Jing Xin, former Jiangxi observation commissioner, was made Jingzhao Prefect.
167
冬十月己酉朔。 戊午，慶成節，賜群臣宴於曲江亭。 辛酉夜，星入斗魁。 前桂管觀察使嚴謇卒。 丙寅，制以敬宗第六男陳王成美為皇太子。 丁丑，太子太保李聽卒。
Winter, tenth month, jiyou new moon. On wuwu, the Qingcheng Festival, a banquet was bestowed on the ministers at Qujiang Pavilion. On the night of xinyou, a star entered the bowl of the Dipper. Yan Jian, former Gui-Guan observation commissioner, died. On bingyin a decree made Chengmei, Prince of Chen and Jingzong's sixth son, Crown Prince. On dingchou Li Ting, Grand Protector of the Crown Prince, died.
168
十一月己卯朔。 壬申，前福建觀察使唐扶卒。 己亥，曲赦京城系囚。
The eleventh month opened on jimao. On renshen Tang Fu, former Fujian observation commissioner, died. On jihai a special pardon was granted to detained prisoners in the capital.
169
十二月己酉朔。 癸丑，貶光祿卿、駙馬都尉韋讓為澧州長史。 乙卯，乾陵火。 以杭州刺史李宗閔為太子賓客，分司東都。 辛酉，上不康，百僚赴延英起居。 乙亥，宰臣入謁，見上於太和殿。 是歲，戶部計見管戶四百九十九萬六千七百五十二。 開成五年春正月戊寅朔，上不康，不受朝賀。 己卯，詔立親弟潁王瀍為皇太弟，權勾當軍國事。 皇太子成美復為陳王。 辛巳，上崩于大明宮之太和殿，壽享三十三。 群臣諡曰元聖昭獻皇帝，廟號文宗。 其年八月十七日，葬于章陵。 【論】史臣曰：昭獻皇帝恭儉儒雅，出於自然，承父兄奢弊之餘，當閽寺撓權之際，而能以治易亂，代危為安。 大和之初，可謂明矣。 初，帝在籓時，喜讀《貞觀政要》，每見太宗孜孜政道，有意於茲。 洎即位之後，每延英對宰臣，率漏下十一刻。 故事，天子雙日視事，帝謂宰輔曰：「朕欲與卿等每日相見，其輟朝、放朝、用雙日可也。」 時憲宗郭后居興慶宮，曰太皇太后，敬宗寶曆太后及上母蕭太后，時呼「三宮太后」。 帝性仁孝，三宮問安，其情如一。 嘗內園進櫻桃，所司啟曰：「別賜三宮太后。」 帝曰：「太后宮送物，焉得為賜。」 遽取筆改賜為奉。 宗正寺以祭器杇敗，請易之，及有司呈進，命陳於別殿，具冠帶面閱之，容色淒然。 尤勤於政理凡選內外群官，府進名，帝必面訊其行能，然後補除。 中書用鴻臚卿張賈為衢州刺史，賈好博，朝辭日，帝謂之曰：「聞卿善長行。」 對曰：「政事之餘，聊與賓客為戲，非有所妨。」 帝曰：「豈有好之而無妨也！」 內外聞之悚息。 而帝以累世變起禁闈，尤側目於中官，欲盡除之。 然訓、注狂狡之流，制禦無術，矢謀既誤，幾致顛危。 所謂「有帝王之道，而無帝王之才」，雖旰食焦憂，不能弭患，異哉！
The twelfth month opened on jiyou. On guichou Wei Rang, Director of the Court of Splendid Happiness and Prince-Consort Commandant, was demoted to chief clerk of Lizhou. On yimao there was a fire at Qianling. Li Zongmin, prefect of Hangzhou, was made Prince's Guest, assigned to the eastern capital. On xinyou the Emperor was unwell, and the hundred officials went to Yanying to inquire after him. On yihai the chief ministers entered to pay respects and saw the Emperor in Taihe Hall. That year Revenue counted 4,996,752 registered households under administration. Kaicheng 5 opened in spring, first month, on the wuyin new moon; the Emperor was unwell and did not receive court congratulations. On jimao an edict established his younger brother Chan, Prince of Ying, as Imperial Younger Brother, with authority to manage military and state affairs. Crown Prince Chengmei was restored as Prince of Chen. On xinsi the Emperor died in Taihe Hall of Daming Palace, aged thirty-three. The assembled ministers gave him the posthumous title Yuansheng Zhaoxian Huangdi and the temple name Wenzong. On the seventeenth day of the eighth month of that year, he was buried at Zhangling. The historian said: Emperor Zhaoxian was naturally respectful, frugal, and refined. He inherited the extravagance and abuses of his father and elder brother and ruled when eunuchs were disrupting authority, yet he was able to exchange disorder for order and turn danger into stability. At the beginning of Taihe, he may indeed be called enlightened. At first, when the Emperor was a regional prince, he liked to read Zhenguan Essentials of Governance; whenever he saw Taizong's diligence in government, he set his mind on it. After he ascended the throne, his Yanying audiences with chief ministers usually lasted until the water clock had dropped eleven marks. By old practice the emperor handled affairs on even-numbered days; the Emperor told the chief ministers, "I wish to see you every day. Court recesses, dismissals, and the use of even-numbered days can continue as before." At that time Xianzong's Empress Guo lived in Xingqing Palace and was called Grand Empress Dowager; Jingzong's Baoli Empress Dowager and the Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiao, were called the "Three Palace Empress Dowagers." The Emperor was benevolent and filial, and he showed the same feeling when asking after each of the three palaces. Once, when cherries were presented from the inner garden, the responsible office reported, "Separately grant them to the Three Palace Empress Dowagers." The Emperor said, "When sending things to the empress dowagers' palaces, how can it be called a grant?" He immediately took up a brush and changed "grant" to "offer." When the Court of the Imperial Clan asked to replace worn sacrificial vessels and officials presented the new ones, the Emperor had them displayed in a side hall, inspected them in full cap and belt, and looked sorrowful. He was especially diligent in government: whenever offices submitted names for appointments inside or outside the capital, he personally questioned the candidates on conduct and ability before appointing them. When the Secretariat appointed Zhang Jia as prefect of Quzhou, Jia was known for gambling; on the day he took leave at court, the Emperor told him, "I hear you are good at the changxing game." He replied, "After government business, I merely play with guests for amusement; it does no harm." The Emperor said, "How can liking it do no harm?" Those inside and outside the court heard this and were awed into caution. Because disturbances had arisen in the palace precincts over successive reigns, the Emperor was especially wary of the eunuchs and wanted to eliminate them all. Yet men like Xun and Zhu were reckless and cunning, and he had no method for controlling them; once his plan went wrong, it nearly brought disaster. This is what is meant by "having the way of an emperor, but not the talent of an emperor": though he ate late and worried deeply, he could not end the danger. Strange indeed!
170
贊曰：昭獻統天，洪惟令德。 心憤仇恥，志除凶慝。 未殄夔魖，又生鬼蜮。 天未好治，亂何由息。
The appraisal said: Zhaoxian governed under Heaven; great indeed was his fine virtue. His heart burned over vengeance and shame; his will was to remove the wicked. Before the kui and xu monsters were destroyed, ghostly villains arose again. If Heaven did not favor good order, how could disorder cease?
